I am p2 with $2966 and three hotels on the south side. Player 1 is down to $34 and heavily invested in light blues and utilities. I have two get-out-of-jail-free cards.

Player 1 cannot reach my pink hotels next roll. From Kentucky Avenue, the maximum roll of 12 lands near the middle of the board, well short of the pinks on the opposite side.

I can reach Park Place with four houses on a roll of 12. I have enough cash to cover that rent and even a Boardwalk hotel. I am now considering whether to unmortgage any properties.

Unmortgaging Pennsylvania Railroad costs $110 for only about $25 in rent. Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue costs $99 with no rent benefit since I lack the orange set. Both are poor investments.

I am now considering a trade. Player 1 has $34 and dangerous properties, but I do not want to give them the orange monopoly. I am checking if they can sell buildings to survive a pink hotel hit. Oriental Avenue with four houses is worth only about $100 in cash.

Vermont Avenue with four houses is worth about $100. Selling a hotel returns half its purchase price, but standard rules require four replacement houses or the property drops to zero buildings.

I recall that selling a hotel previously converted it to four houses, which could then be sold for cash. The bank currently has seventeen houses and eight hotels remaining.

Player 1 can break the Connecticut hotel and sell it for $25. That converts the property to four houses, satisfying even-build requirements. They could then sell those houses evenly for $25 each.

Selling the Connecticut hotel returns $25 and four houses. Those four houses can be sold for $100 total. The light blue properties could liquidate to roughly $325. Dark blue houses sell for $100 each.

Dark blue liquidation totals roughly $700. Combined with light blue sales, player 1 could raise about $1025 from buildings alone. Adding their $34 cash brings total liquidity to approximately $1059. That covers one Virginia hotel hit of $900, leaving them with about $159 and no buildings.

Player 1 can survive a second pink hotel hit. After liquidating buildings, their bare monopolies would pay only about $12 to $16 in rent, which is manageable. The strategy of one pink hotel killing them is unlikely to work.

A single pink hotel hit leaves player 1 with roughly $9 cash and intact light blue buildings. Their dark blue monopolies would drop to unimproved rent of $70 and $100, which I can easily afford. The kill strategy now requires two pink hits before they can rebuild. I am now checking whether they can afford to rebuild after stripping their properties.

I will not give player 1 cash or the orange monopoly. Selling my hotels would reduce rent and help them survive, so I will keep them. I am now looking for a useful trade from them.

Player 1 will not trade away their light blue or dark blue properties, since those are their only weapons. I already hold the pink monopoly with hotels, so giving them Tennessee would let them build orange houses and create another rent threat. They lack the cash to do that immediately.

I rejected a trade for Park Place and Boardwalk. Player 1 would not give up their dark blue houses for mortgaged Tennessee. I do not need more mortgaged properties. The winning strategy is patience. I will keep my pink hotels and cash cushion. I will wait for player 1 to land on the pinks twice.

I can reach Park Place with a roll of 12 and pay $1300. I would still have $1666 left. Boardwalk is unreachable this turn. Player 1 is on Kentucky Avenue. Their next roll from there lands on mortgaged properties or the jail.

Player 1 owns almost the entire board, so landing on their own mortgaged properties is harmless. Go to Jail would give them a safe haven from my pink hotels. I will end the turn without trading.

Rejected trades would waste an action and reveal strategy. I will not propose any.

I now see that going to jail is actually a strategic advantage. While player 1 keeps rolling, I stay safe from their dark blue properties. I might even want to land on the jail space if I can.

I will not trade away my get-out-of-jail-free cards. They have option value, and giving them to player 1 would let that player escape jail and threaten my pink hotels. I will end the turn.
